+## Why Total labeled to date and the 30-day counts differ
+
+These metrics measure different things. Total labeled to date is a current count of files. The 30-day counts show labeling activity.
+
+### Total labeled to date is lower than the 30-day count
+
+This difference is expected when:
+
+- Some files were labeled more than once, for example a label was applied and then changed.
+- Labeled files were deleted. Their earlier activity still appears in the 30-day count.
+
+### Total labeled to date is higher than the 30-day count
+
+This difference is expected when:
+
+- The policy has been on for more than 30 days, so earlier labeling is outside the 30-day window. The displayed turn-on date can show the most recent edit instead of the first time the policy was turned on.
+- Recent activity hasn't appeared yet. Activity data can take time to appear. For more information, see [Get started with Activity explorer](data-classification-activity-explorer).
+
+Total labeled to date might stay higher after a few days for a policy that was turned on less than 30 days ago. If so, contact Microsoft Support.

 Review failure reasons even when few files fail. Transient infrastructure failures are retried automatically, but configuration, protection, or file format failures might require action regardless of volume. Some unsupported files require no action. +## Group membership changes during the activation window
+
+Removing a user from a security group included in a policy might not immediately stop risk scoring for that user. Membership changes can take time to process. Until the service processes the change, activities can continue to receive risk scores and contribute to alerts.
+
+Once the service determines that the user is no longer included in the policy, scoring and alerting stop for that policy. New activities no longer generate or update alerts for that policy.
+
+The service continues to collect and store activities for the remainder of the user's existing activation window. These activities can appear in Activity Explorer. Group removal doesn't automatically remove existing alerts or their previously captured data.
+
+An exception applies to these policy templates when the user's account has already been deleted:
+
+- *Data theft by departing users*
+- *Security policy violations by departing users*
+
+For these deleted accounts, the service can't verify whether the user is still included in the policy. Monitoring continues during the remaining activation window. Activities received during that window can still result in alerts.
+
 ## Configure policy timeframes
 
 1. In Insider Risk Management settings, select **Policy timeframes**.

englishSummary.adminImpact: Administrators should account for continued scoring, alerting, and activity retention after group removal when interpreting alerts and Activity Explorer data. No configuration change is required.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Purview: Adaptive scopes add lifecycle status evaluation controls for recipients and site owners
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Purview is updating adaptive scopes to evaluate only active recipients and site owners by default, with options to include inactive or soft-deleted ones. This includes ISO 8601 duration support in queries. Rollout starts December 2026 (preview) and April 2027 (general availability). No immediate action required.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated November 13, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

What and why

Microsoft Purview is introducing lifecycle status evaluation controls for adaptive scopes. This update gives administrators explicit control over whether active, inactive, and soft-deleted recipients and site owners are included in adaptive scope membership.

With this change, newly created adaptive scopes will evaluate only active recipients and site owners by default. Administrators can configure adaptive scopes to include inactive and/or soft-deleted recipients and site owners when needed.

This update also adds support for ISO 8601 duration values for selected date attributes in the adaptive scope advanced query builder.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 568785.

Rollout schedule

  • Public Preview: Beginning in December 2026 (previously mid-September) and expected to complete in December 2026 (previously early October)
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in April 2027 (previously mid-October 2026) and expected to complete in April 2027 (previously mid-November 2026)

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Microsoft Purview administrators who create or manage adaptive scopes.
  • Organizations that use adaptive scopes for Microsoft Purview policy targeting.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Purview
  • Adaptive Scopes

What will happen

Existing adaptive scopes will continue to function as they do today and will not be automatically modified as part of this rollout.

For newly created adaptive scopes:

  • Active recipients and site owners will be evaluated by default.
  • Inactive and soft-deleted recipients or site owners will not be included unless explicitly configured by an administrator.

Administrators will also have the option to update existing adaptive scopes to use explicit lifecycle status evaluation criteria for recipients and site owners.

Additionally, adaptive scopes will support ISO 8601 duration values for certain date-based attributes in the advanced query builder.

Action required and recommendations

No action is required before rollout.

We recommend that administrators:

  • Review current adaptive scope configurations and governance requirements.
  • Determine whether inactive or soft-deleted recipients and site owners should be included in future adaptive scope definitions.
  • Update adaptive scope creation processes and documentation, if applicable, to account for the new lifecycle status settings.

Learn more

  • (to be updated closer to general availability): Adaptive scopes | Microsoft Purview | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations

No compliance considerations have been identified.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Purview | Information Protection: Sensitivity labels for Microsoft Entra security groups
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Purview will enable sensitivity labels for Microsoft Entra cloud security groups starting mid-January 2027. This allows applying label-based governance and access policies to these groups, enhancing protection and compliance. Admins must enable this feature separately and ensure proper licensing; labels cannot yet be changed or removed once applied.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated November 13, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

What and why

Microsoft Purview is introducing sensitivity labels for Microsoft Entra cloud security groups. This capability extends label-based protection currently available for Microsoft 365 groups and SharePoint sites to cloud security groups.

With this change, organizations can apply published Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels directly to security groups and automatically enforce membership and guest access policies when groups are created or labeled. This helps administrators apply governance policies consistently across group types, reduce the risk of oversharing, and support controlled self-service group creation.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 568217.

Rollout schedule

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in mid-January 2027 (previously mid-November 2026) and expected to complete in mid-January 2027 (previously late November 2026)

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Microsoft Entra administrators
  • Microsoft Purview administrators
  • Organizations that use or plan to use sensitivity labels to govern access to Microsoft Entra security groups

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Purview
  • Microsoft Entra ID
  • Microsoft Entra admin center
  • Azure portal
  • Microsoft Graph
  • PowerShell

What will happen

  • Administrators will be able to apply published Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels to cloud security groups during group creation or after a group has been created.
  • Labels can be assigned through the Microsoft Entra admin center, Azure portal, PowerShell, or Microsoft Graph.
  • Existing sensitivity label functionality for Microsoft 365 groups will remain unchanged.
  • Once a sensitivity label is applied to a security group, the label cannot currently be changed or removed. Support for changing assigned labels will be introduced in a future update.
  • Sensitivity labels can be used to enforce organizational membership and guest access policies for security groups.

Action required and recommendations

No action is required to receive this change.

  • To use sensitivity labels with Microsoft Entra security groups after rollout:
  • Confirm that your organization has eligible licensing, such as Microsoft 365 E3 or Microsoft 365 E5, which includes Microsoft Entra ID P1.
  • In the Microsoft Purview portal, publish the sensitivity labels you want to use with the Groups & Sites scope enabled.
  • Allow up to 24 hours for labels to synchronize and become available in Microsoft Entra ID.
  • Enable sensitivity label support for cloud security groups in your tenant settings.
  • If sensitivity labels are already enabled for Microsoft 365 groups, note that cloud security groups require a separate configuration setting and must be enabled independently.

Consider reviewing your existing sensitivity label policies and governance processes before enabling this feature, particularly because assigned labels cannot currently be changed or removed from security groups.

Learn more

  • Assign sensitivity labels to Microsoft Entra security groups | Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn
  • Learn about sensitivity labels | Microsoft Purview | Microsoft Learn
  • Use sensitivity labels to protect collaborative workspaces (groups and sites) | Microsoft Purview | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations

QuestionAnswer
Does the change modify or add to Purview-related capabilities?Yes. This update extends Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels to Microsoft Entra security groups, adding a new governance and protection capability for this group type.
Does the change include an admin control?Yes. Administrators must enable sensitivity label support for cloud security groups and manage label publication and assignment through Microsoft Purview and Microsoft Entra administrative controls.
Does the change alter how admins manage or demonstrate compliance activities?Yes. Administrators can use sensitivity labels on cloud security groups to apply and enforce access governance policies, expanding the scope of compliance controls available within Microsoft Purview.
